blocks.content: Zero hour is an Indian innovation in the field of parliamentary procedures and has been in existence since 1962.

items: Zero Hour is not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure, unlike the Question Hour.
A Censure Motion must state the specific grounds for its adoption, whereas a No-Confidence Motion does not require stating reasons.
Starred questions require oral answers and permit supplementary questions, whereas unstarred questions require written answers with no supplementaries allowed.
Adjournment Motion involves an element of censure against the government and is not available to the Rajya Sabha.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Question Hour is the first hour of every parliamentary sitting where members ask questions and ministers give answers.
Zero Hour is an informal device not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure, enabling members to raise matters without prior notice.
A No-Confidence Motion can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha with the support of at least 50 members.
Adjournment Motion is an extraordinary device used to draw the attention of the House to a definite matter of urgent public importance.
Quorum is the minimum presence required (1/10th of total membership) for the House to conduct its proceedings.
